Whether the store resets the step number for a new lecture is not visible here.

terms.meaning: The ordered list of lesson steps that the backend creates for a run.
One lesson page, with a title, explanation, and optional extras.
A strip that fills as the user moves through the lesson.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the lecture screen
sections.what: Brings in the animation library, the store, the Button component, and the arrow and book icons.
sections.why: Lists everything the lecture screen needs.

sections.name: LecturePanel (part 1)
sections.title: Current step and navigation limits
sections.what: Reads the lecture and the current step from the store, shows nothing if there is no lecture, works out the total number of steps, and defines the Next and Previous actions, which stop at the first and last step.
sections.why: Likely reason: the limits stop the user moving past the start or end of the lesson.
sections.watch_out: The current step is looked up directly in the list, so a number past the end gives no step and breaks the card below.

sections.name: LecturePanel (part 2)
sections.title: Header, progress, and formula toggle
sections.what: Draws the heading, the Step X of Y label, a progress bar that fills as the user advances, the step card with its number badge and title, the explanation, and the formula show or hide button.
sections.why: Likely reason: showing position and progress tells the user how far through the lesson they are.
sections.watch_out: The formula toggle is one setting shared by every step, so once hidden it stays hidden as the user moves on.

sections.name: LecturePanel (part 3)
sections.title: Formula, example, breakdown, and context
sections.what: Shows the formula box when open, with a fade, then the worked example, the cost breakdown list with name, description and percentage, and the real-world context note. Each part appears only if the step includes it.
sections.why: Likely reason: steps differ in content, so each extra part is optional.
sections.watch_out: Breakdown rows are identified by their name, so two rows with the same name would confuse the list.

sections.name: LecturePanel (part 4)
sections.title: Previous, Next, and step dots
sections.what: Draws the Previous and Next buttons, greyed out at the ends, and one dot per step. The current step's dot is a wider green bar, and clicking a dot jumps straight to that step.
sections.why: Likely reason: the dots give a quick way to see the lesson's length and jump around.
sections.watch_out: Clicking a dot skips the lesson's intended order, so a user may miss earlier steps.

summary: The educational lecture viewer: shows one step at a time of a solar cost lesson, with an explanation, an optional formula, a worked example, a cost breakdown, and real-world context.
purpose: Lets the user learn how the cost numbers were built, one step at a time.
why: Likely reason: a step-by-step lesson helps a non-expert follow the logic from inputs to totals.
how: Reads the lecture steps and the current step number from the store. Shows a progress bar and a card for the current step. The card shows the explanation, then a formula box that can be hidden, a worked example, a cost breakdown table, and context, each only when the step includes it. Previous, Next, and the step dots move between steps.
inputs: Store values: lectureSequence and currentLectureStep. The user's clicks on navigation and the formula toggle.
outputs: The displayed lecture step, and changes to the current step number in the store.
risks: The formula toggle is local to this screen, so it may reset when the panel is shown again. A step number past the end of the list breaks the card.
debug: If the panel crashes, check that the current step number is within the number of steps. A stale number from a previous lecture would point past the end. If a formula or example looks wrong, check the stored step text itself.
